chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, from Jameel, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'From what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has specially granted the believer is that He makes him recognize the righteousness of his brethren, even if it is little.'
And righteousness is not defined by abundance.
And that is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says in His Book:
And they give preference over themselves, even though there is poverty for them.
Then He said: 'And whoever is preserved from the niggardliness of his soul, those are the successful ones.'

And whoever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, makes recognize with that, Allah will love him; and whoever Allah, Blessed and High, loves, He will fulfill his reward on the Day of Resurrection without reckoning.
Then he said: 'O Jameel! Report this hadith to your brethren, for it arouses desire regarding righteousness.'

key_terms.إخوَان: Brethren, referring to fellow believers or companions
key_terms.بِرّ: Righteousness, kindness, or goodness in conduct towards others
key_terms.بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ: Without reckoning, meaning abundant reward beyond strict calculation
key_terms.شُحّ: Niggardliness, stinginess, or greed of the soul
key_terms.مُفْلِحُونَ: The successful ones, those who attain salvation

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of recognizing righteousness in others according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights that true faith is distinguished by the capacity to recognize and practice righteousness (birr) with fellow believers, prioritizing spiritual quality over quantitative abundance. He links this virtue to the Quranic concept of selflessness (ithar), where those who overcome their soul's stinginess are deemed successful and are loved by Allah, receiving an uncalculated reward on the Day of Judgment. This hadith serves as a practical encouragement for believers to cultivate deep, meaningful connections with their community rather than superficial interactions.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from umar Bin Abdul Aziz, from Jameel, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I heard himasws saying: ‘From what Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Specialised the Momin with, is that he recognises the righteousness with his brethren, and even if it was little;
and the righteousness is not with the abundance,
and that is because Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Saying in His<sup>azwj</sup> Book
[59:9] and they are preferring (them) over their own selves and even though poverty was with them’.
Then Heazwj Said [59:9] and whoever is preserved from the niggardliness of his soul, these it is that are the successful ones;

and the one whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Recognises with that, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Love him, and the one whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Loves, He<sup>azwj</sup> would Fulfil his Recompense on the Day of Judgement without a Reckoning’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Jameel! Report this Hadeeth to your brethren, for it arouses desire regarding the righteousness’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz from Jamil from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Of the special characteristics that Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has given to a believer is that he is the means for the recognition and identification of the good deeds of his brothers (in belief) even if such deeds are small and little.
as it is mentioned in the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, in His book:
‘They give preference to them over themselves, even concerning the things that they themselves urgently need. . . .’
then He has said, ‘. . . whoever controls his greed will have everlasting happiness.’ [59:9]

To whoever Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, grants such recognition He loves him. Whomever Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, loves, He grants him reward in full measures on the Day of Judgment and without keeping any counts.’
The Imam said, ‘O Jamil, narrate this Hadith to your brothers (in belief); it is an exhortation to good deeds.’”
